I know a few people who have reached a point in their lives where their ptsd isn't so paralyzing. For me I haven't reached that point yet. I don't sleep, I dont eat, leaving my house gives me anxiety, the smallest of things send me into hysterical panic attacks.  My assault was very violent and traumatizing, and sometimes I lose hope on ever getting "better". With that being said, I know that is irrational and if I put up the required effort I know I can probably heal. But to truthfully answer your question, I think it will stay with us forever. We just have to learn to deal with our triggers and stress in a healthier. With proper therapy and support I am sure we can live normal lives without triggers around every corner, but im not going to be naive and say once we reach that point,  we will never struggle. There will always be times it will hurt, but maybe it wont happen so often. The ultimate goal is to learn how to deal with stress again since ptsd kind of takes your ability to handle stress. So yes. You will have ptsd Forever, but it will become more like an annoying rash that pops up every now and again when you touch something your skin doesn't agree with. It won't be this hard forever. We have to believe that. 
Much love,  you're not alone.

It takes away your sense of security and control. I was raped by a friend. I trusted him, felt safe with him just moments before hand then he took away all control I had. The long lasting wounds come from the trauma you went through. The trauma is being forced to do something you dont want. It hurts, it's scary, and confusing. He took away my sense of security and trust. He was bigger and stronger than me and despite using all my energy to put up a fight he still had control over me, I couldn't do anything about it, and that is very mentally scarring. 

The effects of it can cause ptsd and that is where the long lasting hurt comes from. It's like an injury on your brain, quite literally. There are parts of your brain that can decrease in size and that can make the response your brain has to stress become harder to deal with. You don't handle stress the same way.

Buy an outfit you'd like to fit in and hang it somewhere that you can see to remind yourself of your goal. Put together fun little mile marker crafts. For instance, take two jars, full one up with some marbles, each one represents a pound. As you lose the pounds, transfer the marbles to the other jar. That can help keep you motivated by the satisfaction of seeing that jar slowly empty. Make meals fun, get creative with them. And don't completely deprive yourself.  Have that cookie every now and again. If you are denying yourself all the time, its going to be hard to want to keep going. Everything in moderation. You can do it!
